text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: multiple 'inference-queue' pages fired (eu-west-1). 5xx rate spike on embeddings-worker, 100+ failures/minute. PD: P1.

pagerbot: @Anna K, @Mike R, @Sasha, @Jordan — you’re on the rotation. Claim with `pagerbot claim` to acknowledge.

Anna K: claimed — Anna K here. Acked the page. Investigating initial scope.

Anna K: quick check — is this customer-visible latency or internal retries? Jordan, any CS signals?

Jordan: seeing a handful of customers pinging support, some timeouts on embedding lookups in prod (customer-facing). Not widespread yet but a few major orgs. Adding logs from convo: "hey our search is failing intermittently".

Sasha: jumping in. pulling k8s metrics and the embeddings-worker logs now. Initial glance: KV cache eviction storms + repeated 502 from dedicated GPU pool. Could be a downstream model causing overloaded workers.

Mike R: checking infra. autoscaler shows a large surge in queue depth ~09:42 UTC, but scaling didn’t keep up — some pods OOM and restarted. NVMe pressure on the dedicated pool node group.

Anna K: OK. Priority: (1) prevent more customer impact (2) stabilize queue (3) preserve traces for root cause. Proposing temporary actions: route embedding requests to fallback-quantized model variant in us-east while EU scales, and increase max-concurrency per pod to reduce queue depth. Thoughts?

Sasha: +1 to routing fallback. I can flip routing policy to prefer fallback model variant for new requests. Will do a canary switch for 10% first. Command:

```bash
# quick routing change via infra CLI (canary 10%)
redwoodctl routes update inference --selector embeddings --route fallback-quantized --weight 10
```

Mike R: I’ll add node pool buffer and increase replicas for embeddings-worker in eu-west-1. Running:

```bash
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/embeddings-worker --replicas=20
# bump autoscaler min to 15
redwoodctl autoscaler set embeddings-worker --min 15 --max 60 --region eu-west-1
```

Sasha: making the 10% canary flip now. Will monitor error rate and token failure rate.

incident-bot: change recorded: route update requested by Sasha at 09:45:12 UTC.

Anna K: Sasha — after 2 minutes what’s the error delta? If no increase, push to 50% then 100% and finish drain of overloaded pods. If errors spike, rollback.

Sasha: 09:47 UTC: canary looks good — embeddings failure rate dropped from 12% -> 8% on canary traffic, overall still ~10% due to existing queued requests hitting bad instances. Increasing to 50%.

Mike R: replicas spun up to 20, but seeing 3 pods in CrashLoopBackOff due to an NFS mount flake. I’m cordoning flakey nodes and draining pods off them. Also temporarily disabling node-local NVMe cache writes to reduce I/O pressure.

Anna K: Good. Jordan — please prepare a short customer-facing status note we can send to affected customers: brief, honest, ETA for mitigation. Keep it to two lines + link to status page.

Jordan: on it. Draft: "We’re seeing intermittent search/embedding failures in EU. Engineers have routed new requests to a fallback model and scaled workers; we expect progressive recovery in the next 10–20 minutes. Status updates: https://status.redwood.example/incident/1758881234" — ok to post?

Anna K: OK to post. Do it now and ping me once published. Mark include :loudspeaker:.

Jordan: posted and pinged customers who opened tickets.

Sasha: 09:55 UTC: moving routing to 100% fallback-quantized. Observability: 5xx rate is trending down — from 12% to 2.1% overall. Token latency slightly higher (~40ms) on fallback but acceptable.

Mike R: eu-west infra stabilized after draining bad nodes. No more OOM restarts after parameter tweak (reduced batch size on worker). Disk pressure cleared.

Anna K: Great. Next: let’s capture core dumps and a full netstat + JVM heap snapshot from the three CrashLoopBackOff pods before they get terminated. Sasha/Mike take them — store artifacts in the incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1758881234/artifacts.

Sasha: running snapshots now. Paste of useful diagnostics I ran:

```text
# last 50 lines from embeddings-worker stderr
2026-03-15T09:44:51Z ERROR model-infer: OOM when allocating kv-cache 1.2GB
2026-03-15T09:45:03Z WARN retry: backend 10.0.8.12 responded 502 Bad Gateway
2026-03-15T09:46:30Z INFO routing: fallback-quantized weighted 10 -> 50
```

Mike R: uploaded node diagnostics and nvme SMART logs to the bucket.

Anna K: OK — reduction in customer impact. I’d like a short postmortem stub: who did what, timeline, why fallback helped, and follow-ups (autoscaler bug, NVMe config hygiene, model memory regression). Sasha/Mike/Jordan — can you add follow-ups to the incident tracker? Tag me for review.

Sasha: adding follow-ups now. Items: 1) investigate KV cache memory spike root cause (likely model change) 2) autoscaler min not honored (race condition) 3) node provisioning template - NVMe mount options.

Neil: quick note — we should add a temporary alert to catch model memory regressions: increase sensitivity on kv-cache usage and trigger before OOM. I’ll file that with infra alerts.

Anna K: thanks. Last status: 10:02 UTC — stable, error rates low, customers notified. I’m closing the active handoff in 15 min unless something else pops. For now, keep the 100% fallback in place until a safe model rollback or model patch.

pagerbot: @Anna K acknowledged the page and marked incident status: triaged -> mitigated.

Anna K: ending note — big props to the team for the quick routing play and buffer-scale. Will follow up with a timeline and assign owners for the three follow-ups. If anyone sees a regression, reopen this thread. :thumbsup:

Sasha: leaving a short playbook addition: add "route to fallback-quantized" as first mitigation step for embeddings-worker P1s. I’ll PR to runbook.

incident-bot: incident closed (mitigated) at 10:12:45 UTC by Anna K. Artifacts: s3://redwood-incidents/1758881234/artifacts.

Anna K: thanks all — end of thread."
